extra_discoveries:
MYSTERY SOLVED (if-<= SIGILL vs for-<= no crash). Root cause: Typechecker::second_relation_token_chains (Typechecker.cpp:203-243) falls off the end of a non-void function (g++ -Wreturn-type at line 243; g++ emits ud2 -> SIGILL). gdb backtrace of `if (a <= b)` ends at Typechecker.cpp:227 inside second_relation_token_chains, called from feed_in_tokens:98, parse_relation:2264, parse_if_statement:1643. That function is only reached from feed_in_tokens (Typechecker.cpp:98) when first_token!=NULL, second_token==NULL, the fed token is a relationship token, and relation_tokens.size()==1.

WHY IF CRASHES: parse_base_statement calls set_statement_type(T_IF) which calls clear_tokens(false) (Typechecker.cpp:56) right before the condition, so the accumulator is empty. Feeding `a`->first_token; `<`->relation_tokens[0] (size 0->1); `=`->relation_tokens.size()==1 so second_relation_token_chains(=) is called with relation_tokens[0]==T_LESS, which hits `case T_LESS: break;` and falls off -> UB. gdb at Typechecker.cpp:98 confirmed first=278(id a), second=999(null), relsz=1, relation_tokens[0]=60('<').

WHY FOR DOES NOT CRASH: parse_loop_statement parses the initializer assignment `i := 0` FIRST and never clears the typechecker between the initializer and the condition. The literal `0` is left sitting in first_token. So when the condition's first operand `i` is fed, first_token is already non-NULL and `i` lands in second_token; the relationship operator `<` is then fed while second_token!=NULL, missing the (first!=NULL && second==NULL && relationship) branch and falling into the terminal `else {/* too many tokens */}` (Typechecker.cpp:120-123), silently DROPPED. relation_tokens never reaches size 1, so second_relation_token_chains is never called. gdb feed-trace of the for-loop: feed=60('<') occurs with second(before)=278 already set -> dropped; a breakpoint on second_relation_token_chains never fires and the program exits 0.

GENERALIZATION (mapped empirically): if-conditions/standalone relations using `<=`, `>=`, `==`, and `!=` ALL SIGILL (exit 132) — every two-token relational operator whose first relation token (`<`,`>`,`=`,`!`) then chains with `=`. Single `<` and `>` never crash (they push only one relation token, size 0->1, returning before the chaining branch). The SAME operators inside for-conditions never crash (le/ge/eq all exit 0) due to the leftover-token mechanism above. Net: no if-statement using <=, >=, ==, or != can be compiled, and for-loop condition type-checking is effectively dead (operator+operands dropped). This one fall-off-end function is the shared root cause of claim 3's control-case crash and the enum `==` crash seen while probing claim 11.

OTHER DISCOVERIES:
1. TYPE_INT mis-registration (separate parser/symbol-table bug): a local `variable localFlag : bool` reads back identifier_data_type=TYPE_INT (gdb at check_return_statement for c7_boolret). This is what makes bool locals crash on return (claim 7B) and would corrupt any bool-local type comparison elsewhere.
2. convert_to_typechecker_types (Typechecker.cpp:1251-1295) has no TYPE_NONE case and no default (g++ -Wswitch at line 1256), so it returns an UNINITIALIZED typechecker_types for enum/none-typed identifiers; that value flows into check_if_statement/check_loop_statement. `if (enumvar)` would branch on an indeterminate type.
3. SymbolTable::create_new_scope_table (SymbolTable.cpp:172) also falls off the end of a non-void function (g++ -Wreturn-type) — out of this batch's scope but flagged.
4. token::identifier_data_type (token.h:126) has no default initializer (unlike every other member), so a default-constructed token's data type is indeterminate.
overall_notes:
All 9 claims in batch D were verified by fresh reading of Typechecker.cpp / parser.cpp / token.h, by compiler warnings (-Wall -Wextra -Wswitch -Wreturn-type on a scratch copy), and by building the compiler in /tmp/claude-1000/-datadrive-data-compiler-course/e0905122-5395-4b36-add9-f6a81e41bd28/scratchpad/verify-D and running minimal .src probes (probes/*.src) plus gdb. 8 of 9 CONFIRMED; only typechecker.4 is PARTIAL (the 'bypass ALL type validation' scope is overstated — base-type incompatibility is still caught; the real, confirmed defect is that the integer-only rule for &/| is never enforced). typechecker.11 was upgraded from the agent's SPECULATIVE tag to a reproduced runtime confirmation.

Cross-claim root causes worth Blake's attention: (a) the feed_in_tokens two-slot+relation_tokens state machine underlies claims 1, 2, 3 and the SIGILL mystery — synthesized relation types are never propagated (only the rightmost raw operand token is), and leftover/uncleared state or a leading unary operator silently disables checking. (b) Two fall-off-end non-void functions (second_relation_token_chains @243, check_return_statement @1211) are hard SIGILL crashes on this g++ -O0 build; second_relation_token_chains makes the compiler unable to compile ANY if-statement using <=, >=, ==, or !=. (c) check_assignment_statement (claim 8) and the missing array handling (claim 5) mean assignment and array typing are essentially unchecked.
